# Credo Behavioral and Customer Engagement

[← Scale AI](../README.md) · [Every Scale AI question](../../scale-ai.md) · [Read it on TrueInterview](https://trueinterview.io/study/credo-behavioral-and-customer-engagement)

---

## What to Expect

- Typical prompts:
  - A project you are proudest of.
  - A difficult project and what made it difficult.
  - Feedback that you received.
  - A project delivered under a tight deadline.
  - A conflict or difference of opinion with a manager.
  - A personal characteristic that might be viewed unfavorably at work, and why you believe you have it.
  - An independent project.
  - Your strengths and areas for improvement.
  - Why you want to join Scale AI.
  - Why you want to leave your current position / why you do not want to keep doing your present daily work.
  - The direction you would like to pursue next.
- Customer-facing versions may ask about your relationship with your current manager and the rating that manager would give you.
- Recruiter screens may request detailed project information, including ML subjects such as GRPO, instead of remaining strictly logistical.

## Guidance

- Build answers around a specific situation, the actions you took, and the result. For Scale's customer-facing positions, broad excitement about AI alone is insufficient.
- Respond calmly to questions about managers and self-evaluation. Do not introduce unexpectedly harsh criticism; describe weaknesses in terms of scope and effect, along with how you are addressing them.
- For project-related questions, connect the example to the position: enterprise AI solution delivery for FDE / enterprise SWE, LLM fundamentals and model development for MLE, and hands-on production ownership for general SWE.

## Preparation

- Draft six STAR stories covering a proud project, conflict, feedback, time pressure, a weakness, and customer or user impact.
- Plan a 60-second response to “why Scale AI” that reflects the target team’s work instead of generic enthusiasm about AI.
- Rehearse responses about manager ratings and weaknesses so they do not come across as defensive.
